aboutPage.bioP1: I'm a creator, a programmer, and a thinker. I love building things from scratch — whether it's a painting, a piece of code, or a deep-dive essay.
aboutPage.bioP2: For the longest time, the biggest obstacle to this passion was my own brain: I have ADHD. After trying nearly every productivity tool on the market, I realized they were all designed for a neurotypical mind. I needed a "partner" — something that understood me and could give me a gentle nudge right when I needed it most.
aboutPage.bioP3: I couldn't find it anywhere. So I decided to build it myself — for me, and for the millions of others with a "busy brain" just like mine. That's how Dopamind was born.

methods.sectionCaption: Step through common solving methods stage by stage — each thumbnail hides everything except the cubies placed by that point.
methods.title: Solving methods

lbl.name: Layer-by-Layer (LBL)
lbl.description: Classic beginner method. Solve one layer at a time — bottom cross, bottom corners, middle edges, then last layer.

cfop.name: CFOP (Fridrich)
cfop.description: Mainstream speedsolving method. Cross builds the bottom cross, F2L pairs corners with middle edges, OLL orients the last face, PLL permutes the last layer.

roux.name: Roux
roux.description: Block-building method. Build a 1×2×3 block on the left, then on the right, solve the last-layer corners (CMLL), then finish with the M-slice and last six edges (LSE).

rouxCard.title: Roux Method
rouxCard.desc: Blocks, two-look CMLL and LSE — every case with a diagram you can open on this cube.

cubeRoux.title: Roux Method (Beginner-Friendly)
cubeRoux.intro: The Roux method has four stages: build the left 1×2×3 block, build the right one, solve the top corners (CMLL), then finish the last six edges with only M and U turns (LSE).

fb.intro: The first block is a 1×2×3 on the left: the DL edge, the two bottom-left corners and their two edges. There are no fixed algorithms — you look, pair a corner with its edge, and insert. These are the hand-moves that come up over and over. Hold the cube with the block on the left and the empty slot at the front.

insert.title: Pairing and inserting
insert.desc: Each case opens in the 3D cube with the pair already in position; watch where the two pieces start and how the turns bring them home without disturbing the rest of the block.

pairLeft.name: Pair on top, left side
pairLeft.hint: Corner above the slot, edge beside it on the left. Move the pair out of the way, open the slot, drop it in.

mSlice.name: Pair with the M slice
mSlice.hint: Corner at the back-left of the top, edge at the right. M brings the edge round to meet it, then F' drops the pair in.

edgeOnTop.name: Corner in the slot, edge on top
edgeOnTop.hint: The corner is already home, the edge sits at the right of the top. Take the corner out to meet it, then F' inserts both.

misPaired.name: Pair on top, colors mismatched
misPaired.hint: Corner and edge are next to each other on the right of the top but don't match. F' opens the slot, re-pair with L' U' L U' L' U L, F' closes it.

sb.intro: The second block mirrors the first on the right — but now the left block must not move. Only R, r, M and U turns are safe. The wide r turn is the Roux trick: it moves the right layer and the M slice together, so you can grab edges from the bottom without touching the left.

insert.title: Pairing and inserting
insert.desc: All four cases keep the left block untouched. The DR edge is assumed solved; these insert the front-right corner-edge pair.

pairRight.name: Pair on top, right side
pairRight.hint: Corner above the slot, edge beside it on the right. The mirror of the first-block insert.

mPair.name: Pair with the M slice
mPair.hint: Edge at the back-left of the top, corner at the right. U then M brings the edge round to the corner, R U' R' inserts the pair.

cornerInSlot.name: Corner in the slot, edge on top
cornerInSlot.hint: The corner is already home, the edge sits on top. U R lifts the corner out, M brings the edge to it, U' R' puts both in.

twistedCorner.name: Corner in the slot, twisted
twistedCorner.hint: The corner sits in its slot but turned. L F' L' flips it out through the left block and back, the M moves fetch the edge, R U' R' inserts.

cmll.intro: With both blocks done, solve the four top corners in one go. Full CMLL has 42 cases; two-look splits it into orient, then permute, and needs only nine algorithms. Because the M slice gets fixed afterwards, these algorithms are free to disturb it. Yellow stickers show where the top color is; a bar on the outside means that corner's top color faces sideways.

orient.title: Step 1 · Orient the corners
orient.desc: Count how many top corners already show the top color. 0 → H or Pi. 1 → S or AS. 2 → U, T or L. Match the pattern and turn the top layer so it lines up with the diagram.

permute.title: Step 2 · Permute the corners
permute.desc: If one side already matches — say both corners on one face are red — turn the top so that pair is on the left, then use the adjacent swap. If no side matches, use the diagonal swap.

adjacent.name: Adjacent swap
adjacent.hint: Put the two corners to swap on the right.

lse.intro: Six edges remain, and only M and U turns are needed. Three steps: orient the edges so every top/bottom color faces up or down (EO), place the UL and UR edges, then finish the last four. Diagrams show the top layer's edges plus the two bottom edges DF and DB; corners are left blank because they are already solved.

eo.title: 4a · Edge orientation
eo.desc: A filled edge has its top/bottom color facing up or down — good. Blank means bad. Count the bad edges on top and bottom; there are only a handful of patterns and M' U M is the move that changes them.

arrow.name: Arrow
arrow.hint: Turn the top so the three bad edges point at the bad bottom edge, then M' U M fixes all four.

twoTwo.name: Split pairs
twoTwo.hint: Shortest solution shown. The by-hand route: M' U2 M turns it into an arrow, then finish as above.

fourZero.name: All on top
fourZero.hint: All four top edges bad. M U2 M swaps a pair down into an arrow, then finish.

twoTop.name: Both on top
twoTop.hint: Not 0, not 4: M' U M makes it four bad edges in arrow shape, U2 to aim, M' U M to finish.

oneOne.name: One up, one down
oneOne.hint: Same idea — the first M U M creates the arrow.

twoBottom.name: Both at the bottom
twoBottom.hint: M U M lifts them into an arrow, then finish as usual.

ulur.title: 4b · UL and UR
ulur.desc: Yellow on top, white on the bottom, red block on the left: the two edges still to place are yellow-red and yellow-orange (framed in the diagrams). Sink both to the bottom so they sit opposite each other, turn the top to line up, then M2 U or M2 U'. The centers end up flipped — the next step fixes that.

bothTop.name: Both on top
bothTop.hint: Turn the top until they're opposite each other (front and back). M2 sinks both, U' lines them up, M2 U' places them.

oneBottom.name: One up, one down
oneBottom.hint: U2 to line up, M U2 M' sends the top one down opposite the other; U' to line up, M2 U brings both up and places them.

bothBottom.name: Both at the bottom
bothBottom.hint: Turn the top to line up, M2 brings them up, U places them.

bothBottomAlt.name: Both at the bottom (other way)
bothBottomAlt.hint: The pair sits the other way round: U2 to line up the top, then M2 U'.

needM2.name: Centers flipped
needM2.hint: The white center is on top: M2 flips it back.

oneWhite.name: One white on top
oneWhite.hint: Turn the top so the white edge is at the front, then swap it with the bottom edge.

twoWhite.name: Two whites on top
twoWhite.hint: Swap top and bottom edges twice, once on each side.

byLook.name: Solve by looking
byLook.hint: No white on top, but the front and back edges are swapped: M2, turn the top, M2 back.

cubeAnalyzer.title: csTimer Analyzer
cubeAnalyzer.intro: Export your sessions from csTimer and drop the file here to see how you're really progressing: rolling averages, PB history, milestones, daily volume and a power-law learning curve. Everything runs in your browser — nothing is uploaded.

howTo.title: How to export from csTimer
howTo.step1: Open cstimer.net and click the gear icon in the top-left corner.
howTo.step2: Scroll to Import / Export and choose "Export to file".

drop.label: Drop your csTimer export here, or click to choose a file
drop.loadSample: Or load my own data as a sample
drop.sample: Sample data: my Roux journey, May–Oct 2026

errors.notJson: That doesn't look like a csTimer export (it isn't valid JSON).
errors.noSessions: No sessions with solves were found in that file.
errors.generic: Couldn't read that file. Please try again.

singles.title: Single solves
singles.desc: Every solve in order. The dark line is the Ao100 trend; highlighted points are new personal bests.

ao.title: Rolling averages (Ao5 / Ao12 / Ao50 / Ao100)
ao.desc: The trend of your recent solves — this is the real measure of progress.

hist.title: Time distribution
hist.desc: How your solve times are spread.

pb.title: Personal best history
pb.desc: Best single / Ao5 / Ao12 / Ao100 over time, stepping down with each new record.

dailyAvg.title: Daily average
dailyAvg.desc: Mean solve time per day — shows good and bad days.

hourly.title: Time of day
hourly.desc: When you practice, by local hour.

speedup.title: Speed-up vs. day one (log₂)
speedup.desc: How many times faster each day is than your first day. +1 = twice as fast, +2 = four times, +3 = eight times. Each step is the same size of improvement.

powerLaw.title: Skill vs. cumulative practice (power law)
powerLaw.desc: Vertical: −ln(daily average seconds). Horizontal: cumulative solves, log scale. The Power Law of Practice predicts a straight line — above the trend is a breakthrough, below it a plateau.

powerLaw.halving: Double the practice → time drops by

band.steady: Steady learning at a high level
band.veryFast: Very fast (early days or a method upgrade)

milestones.title: Milestones
milestones.desc: The first time each series dipped under a threshold, and how many days in that was.

recent.title: Last 20 solves
recent.desc: Your most recent solves in this session.

cubeAnalyzer.footer: Your data never leaves your browser. Built alongside the “solve the cube without memorizing” series.
